scope: The evidence tier. Every forecast the generic learner makes carries a measured error envelope, and this manifest declares what that envelope has to be, where its coverage is measured, and the band that coverage has to land in. It does not measure forecast accuracy, control adequacy, or support outside observed conditions; it measures only whether the declared envelope covers the held-out error it claims to cover.
frozen: This file and its digest constant in glassbox.experimental.harness are frozen and committed before any candidate that reports an envelope is fitted. A band, a nominal level, a channel group, a measurement set, or a reference value changed after coverage was seen fails review. The recipe block below records the recipe this manifest was frozen against; a candidate recipe may differ from it, and every run records the recipe it actually fitted. What this manifest pins about the recipe is the evaluation plan, the information budget every window is cut to, which the harness rederives.

envelope.resolution: one half-width per horizon step and per observation channel, aligned with what predict returns and stated in that channel's own physical units.
envelope.calibration_data: only rows the fit already holds out. The recipe reserves a quarter of the supplied recordings as its development role and caches the development windows cut from them; those windows, and nothing else, calibrate the envelope. No scored row, no training window, and no held-out recording of any tier may enter the calibration in any role.
envelope.estimator: a split-conformal half-width: the finite-sample quantile of the absolute development-window forecast error at that horizon step and channel, at the nominal level. The exact quantile rule belongs to the candidate, not to this manifest; what this manifest pins is the nominal level and the calibration data.
envelope.recalibration: update refits the recipe on the merged training cache and recalibrates on the pinned development cache, so a revision carries an envelope calibrated the same way from the same held-out role.
envelope.known_approximation: the development windows also select the training checkpoint, so they are held out of the gradient but not of model selection. That is a stated approximation of exchangeability, not an independent calibration set, and it is one reason measured coverage may sit outside the band.
envelope.exposure: one method on LearnedDynamics, envelope(horizon_steps), returning the per-step, per-channel half-widths aligned with predict's output, plus the same table in the artifact and in the fit report. There is no caller option: every forecast carries it.

rigid_body_15.applies_to: the fifteen-channel observed contract the platform tier's adapter and the control tier both build: world-frame velocity, body rates, then the nine body-to-world rotation entries in row-major order.

channel_groups.per_channel: for the synthetic families, whose channels are dimensionless coordinates of unrelated systems, each observed channel is its own group.

band.meaning: The declared coverage band around the nominal 0.90. A measured coverage is inside the band when minimum <= coverage <= maximum. A band is a statement about an envelope that was calibrated elsewhere and measured here; it is not a tolerance to widen an envelope into.

coverage.definition: For one measured case, one channel group and one horizon step: the fraction of scored (row, channel) pairs in that group whose absolute forecast error at that horizon step is at or below the envelope half-width for that step and channel. Pooled coverage over every horizon step of the case is reported beside it and does not decide anything.
coverage.rows: Exactly the rows the tier already scores, with no new origins, no new recordings, and no re-fitting: the same predictions the tier saves, read against the same targets.
coverage.saved: Each run saves, beside every prediction array it already saves, an envelope half-width array of the same shape, so a replay never has to trust a recorded coverage number.
coverage.replay: verify rebuilds the half-widths from the saved model artifact, recomputes every coverage number from the saved arrays, and replays this decision. A half-width array that does not match the model's own envelope, or a coverage number that does not match the arrays, rejects the run.

synthetic.measured_on: every declared case and evaluation regime of the synthetic manifest, on its evaluation rows.

platform.measured_on: every pinned corpus's held-out rows, at the recipe's horizon resolved on that corpus's own sample grid.

control.measured_on: the reserved calibration recording, which is never fitted in any role, at every origin that carries the recipe's whole consumed context and the whole horizon after it.

decision.rule: For every declared case of the tier, every declared channel group and every horizon step: the measured coverage lies inside the declared band.
decision.metric: band_excess, the distance the measured coverage lies outside the band: max(0, minimum - coverage, coverage - maximum), and zero for a coverage inside it. It is the smaller-is-better quantity the reference allowance is stated on, exactly as the other tiers state theirs on an RMSE.
decision.gates_from: the first candidate after the one this manifest was frozen for. This first measurement reports coverage and does not decide any run. From the next candidate the band is enforced under the same semantics the platform and control tiers already use: a run is accepted only when no case's band_excess regresses past its reference value times 1.05 plus 0.005, the rule holds on every case the reference already meets it on, and nothing structural fails. A case the reference already fails is reported with gating false, not gated.
decision.structural: Always fails closed when the rule is enforced, whatever the reference says: a declared case missing, duplicated or undeclared, a declared channel group missing, a horizon step count that differs from the tier's own, a coverage that is not a finite number in [0, 1], or a scored-row count of zero.
decision.reported_when_unenforced: Every number and every breach is computed, recorded and printed exactly as it would be when enforced; only the tier's accepted flag ignores it.
decision.meaning: A measurement of held-out coverage for this envelope on these rows. It is not a probabilistic guarantee, not a support envelope, not a claim about conditions no recording covers, and not control adequacy.

reference.metric: band_excess, recomputed from the reference's own recorded coverage and this manifest's band.
reference.meaning: When the reference file exists beside this manifest, no case's band_excess may exceed its reference value times 1.05 plus 0.005. A run copies the reference it compared into its output directory and records its sha256, and verify anchors that copy to the committed file rather than believing it.
reference.gates_the_rule: The same recorded value decides which cases the rule gates. A case whose reference coverage is itself inside the band is a case the reference meets, and the band is a gate there; a case the reference already fails is reported only. With no reference compared there is no case the reference meets, and the rule is reported everywhere.
